answer: A vineyard-agent exchange renews each key only after 1,000,000 sequential SHA-256 steps seeded by that key and an unpredictable epoch beacon. The chain commits to a signed river salinity forecast at the planned tide and the vine salt-tolerance limit; renewal fails if forecast salinity exceeds the limit. Verifiers recompute both chain and safety test. Every extra identity needs a separate chain each epoch even if idle; another key's proof is invalid. Fast hardware can make this work cheap, and it does not prove unique operators.
